asserted_claims: Scoped obstruction to fixed finite prime cutoff plus bounded compact correction.
Explicit all-cutoff smooth pole-neutral negative witness.
No contradiction to RH or to complete support-consistent window methods.
difference: Reuses prior signed jump factorization and earlier pole-neutral cutoff witness from channel_audit.md. Adds an explicit uniform recipe for every finite cutoff and its bounded-compact-correction obstruction. No worldwide novelty claim.
domain: signed Weil quadratic forms and arithmetic translation operators
method: Exact signed jump factorization, full archimedean second moment, mollified polynomial derivative bounds, pole annihilator (d²/du²-1/4), explicit scale 32(1+ceil(log2 X)), weakly vanishing translates and compactness.
next_test: Work with all prime powers required by each actual test support and establish the full signed Weil positivity without a fixed-cutoff compact repair or assuming zero-location information.
object: For every finite prime-power cutoff X>=2, construct smooth pole-neutral f_T with Q_X(f_T)/||f_T||^2<-49/10. For every bounded selfadjoint compact K on L2, translates of this test force Q_X(f)+<f,Kf><0 somewhere.
obligations: The omitted prime-power autocorrelations are not evaluated or given a sign.
Full support-complete signed Weil positivity remains open.
Compactness and boundedness are essential hypotheses, not labels for every possible reservoir.
scope: Fixed finite X and all smooth compactly supported pole-neutral tests. Bounded selfadjoint compact corrections, including bounded finite-rank corrections. Excludes no support-complete window construction, unbounded moment correction, or noncompact/moving-tail mechanism.
stop_condition: Never treat the fixed-cutoff negative witness as an RH counterexample. Stop any attempted global proof that drops the noncompact/mitscaling arithmetic remainder or extends a finite-window result without the required cofinal compatibility.
target: Test whether a fixed finite prime cutoff plus a compact reservoir correction can supply global Weil positivity.
